title: Split-conformal calibration of finite-support Wasserstein ambiguity radii

source.service_catalog_note: The service catalog is checked structurally against the pinned NRES-009 source. The Rust evaluator does not recompute a Git object SHA-1.

protocol.method: split-conformal block calibration using W1 between each block's empirical joint-state outcome distribution and its frozen candidate forecast distribution
protocol.calibration_unit: one source-family block; repeated outcomes inside a block form one empirical joint-state distribution and count as one calibration unit
protocol.quantile_rule: k=ceil((m+1)*(1-alpha)); one-based kth order statistic. If k>m the radius is +infinity (serialized as null) and no finite radius is available.
protocol.score_definition: score_b=W1(empirical distribution of observed joint states in block b, frozen forecast distribution for block b), using the declared weighted-Hamming ground metric.
protocol.coverage_claim: If calibration source-family blocks and one future source-family block are exchangeable, conditional on the separately fitted/frozen forecast model and predeclared metric, split-conformal rank calibration gives marginal P(score_future <= radius) >= 1-alpha jointly over calibration blocks and the future block.
protocol.coverage_limit: This guarantee concerns the future block's empirical outcome distribution relative to its block forecast. It does not establish that the unknown population distribution lies in the ball, provide coverage conditional on the realized calibration sample, or survive arbitrary distribution shift.
assumptions: Forecast model, state encoding, ground metric, block-size rule, miscoverage level and calibration split are frozen before calibration outcomes are inspected.
Calibration source-family blocks and one future block are exchangeable at the block level.
Each source family contributes exactly one block to the calibration split.
Calibration and evaluation blocks use the same predeclared block size and forecast horizon.
No source family or observation is duplicated across calibration and evaluation splits.
For the optional population-law sampling correction only, outcomes within each block are conditionally iid from a fixed block-specific joint-state distribution.

ground_metric.name: weighted_hamming
ground_metric.definition: d(s,t)=sum_i w_i*1[s_i!=t_i], with finite strictly-positive weights.

protocol.numerical_method: Successive-shortest-augmenting-path min-cost flow on a finite bipartite transport graph with residual reverse arcs.
protocol.population_correction_assumption: For this optional correction only, observations inside each future block are conditionally iid from a fixed block-specific population distribution over the joint service-state support.

expected_development_diagnostic.interpretation: Public synthetic development diagnostic only; not a confirmatory coverage estimate.

interpretation_guardrails: All blocks, forecasts, outcomes and scores are fictional public-development inputs.
NRES-009 distributions are used as forecast templates only; synthetic block outcomes are separately generated and are not real service outcomes.
Synthetic source-family IDs demonstrate contract checks, not independent custody.
The split-conformal statement requires block exchangeability and applies only to the declared block empirical-distribution score.
No population-law coverage, calibration-conditional guarantee or shift-invariant guarantee is claimed.
The calibrated radius is not evidence of operational coverage.
No decision optimizer, learned loss-aware transport metric or production policy is certified.
No political beliefs, identity, loyalty, personal suitability or natural-person attributes are collected or scored.

expected_population_correction.interpretation: Under a conditional-iid-within-block assumption, add a distribution-free finite-state sampling-error allowance to the conformal empirical-block radius. The resulting population-law ball reaches the complete support diameter in this small-block fixture and is therefore vacuous.
